newsitem.title: USA: CCB to acquire American Federal for $325 million.
newsitem.headline: CCB to acquire American Federal for $325 million.

text.p: CCB Financial Corp. said Tuesday it signed an agreement to acquire American Federal Bank FSB in a stock deal worth $325.1 million. The news sparked a sharp rise in American Federal's stock.
Under the agreement, American Federal stockholders would receive 0.445 shares of CCB's common stock for each share they own, which valued the stock at $28.86 a share.
The combination of Durham, N.C.-based CCB and Greenville, S.C.-based American Federal will form a financial institution with $6.9 billion in assets and $5.5 billion in deposits, CCB said.
Following the announcement, American Federal's stock jumped $6 to $27.125 on the Nasdaq market, while CCB was off $1.625 to $66.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.

While the acquisition would boost CCB's assets and deposits as well as give it a new robust market in neighbouring South Carolina, CCB remains just one of three mid-tier banks based in North Carolina, analysts said.
CCB spokesman John Ramsey called the shift into South Carolina a "natural extension" even though the goal was not to reach into the deep pockets of big business.

"We're primarily a consumer and small business bank, as is American Federal," he said. "While those (big) businesses are growing, people are moving in; and big businesses spawn a whole host of smaller businesses, and as those markets expand we have opportunities there, too."

The deal would expand the CCB franchise from its base in Durham down the Interstate 85 corridor that runs through South Carolina's dynamic markets. The area is the U.S. base for German carmaker Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG as well as French tiremaker Michelin SA and Flagstar Cos. Inc.
John Coffey, an analyst at Robinson-Humphrey, said the price of the acquisition was high but strategically the two institutions make a good fit.
"The price looks high but American Federal is not an ordinary thrift," he said. "It's a bank-like company and is getting a bank-like price."
CCB has 161 banking offices in North Carolina, while American Federal operates 40 banking offices in northwest South Carolina.
The transaction, which is subject to stockholders' approval, is expected to be completed by the third quarter this year.
